claims: A fee-in-pool CPMM batch has an exact telescoping K identity: final K equals initial K plus the sum of per-step fee-aware K gaps.
Each single-step K gap decomposes into an integer-division remainder plus a fee-retention bonus.
Positive reserves are preserved across fee-aware batches, and any positive trade under a positive fee rate strictly increases K.
Batch execution composes as a list action, and the K-gap sum splits additively across sub-batches.
Input-side and output-side accounting identities recover gross input volume, total output, and K-gap certificates from boundary data.
The K value after a single fee-in-pool swap is monotone in the fee rate under the declared bps cap.

Concrete witnesses cover batch composition, retention lower bounds, general strict monotonicity, balance-sheet checks, order dependence, single-step behavior, batch telescoping, fee-vs-zero-fee comparison, and zero-fee collapse.
proof_method: list induction over fee-aware CPMM batch execution
Nat ceiling-fee positivity and reserve-preservation lemmas
boundary-data certificate uniqueness via arithmetic cancellation

boundaries: The model covers same-direction fee-in-pool CPMM execution in natural-number arithmetic; runtime code still needs a bridge showing it emits these exact gross amounts, fee calculations, and reserve updates.
The strict K-increase result requires positive reserves, positive trade size, positive fee rate, and fee_bps <= 10000.
The batch order-dependence witness shows this theorem is an accounting certificate, not an order-optimality theorem.
The proof does not establish authorization, oracle freshness, path discovery, cross-pool routing, or settlement attestation validity.
